$description: In2IT EBS design tokens, v2.0. The single source of truth for colour, type, space and state. Every other artefact references these rather than restating them.

brand.$comment: IDENTITY LIVES HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE. The group renames to Enverics, with In2IT EBS continuing as a practice name. Everything below this block is name-independent: the palette is identical in both brand books, and the type, space, state, chart and accessibility rules do not change with the name. A rename is therefore an edit to this block plus new logo artwork — not a new system.
brand.name: In2IT EBS
brand.legal-name: In2IT Enterprise Business Services Private Limited

wordmark-face.note: Never set live. The In2IT EBS wordmark and the Enverics wordmark are different drawings; neither is Newsreader.

colour.$comment: The six core colours are unchanged from v1.0 in intent. Two corrections and two additions, each recorded below.

steel.name: Steel Blue
steel.note: CORRECTED. v1.0 printed HEX #121e3b against RGB 63,117,163 on the colour-codes page. The RGB was right; the HEX was Deep Navy repeated. Anyone who copied the HEX got navy.

sky.name: Light Sky Blue
sky.note: Background and on-navy text only. Never text on white.

sand.name: Muted Sand
sand.note: The one warm note. Its home is ON NAVY (9.73:1), not on white (1.69:1). v1.0 had this backwards.

grey-soft.name: Soft Grey
grey-soft.note: Surface only. 1.31:1 on white — it cannot carry text at any size.

grey-text.name: Slate Grey
grey-text.note: ADDED. v1.0 had no colour for secondary text: Soft Grey is 1.31:1 on white. 5.95:1 on white, so it is the secondary text colour.

steel-light.name: Mist Blue
steel-light.note: ADDED. A mid-blue between Steel and Sky for card fills and chart series. Carries Navy text at 7.87:1 and nothing else.

off-white.name: Paper
off-white.note: ADDED. Soft Grey #E1E1E1 is too heavy for a page background. 15.50:1 with Navy.

colour-on-dark.$comment: Navy is the dominant surface, so it needs its own full set. v1.0 specified none, which is why an undocumented teal was invented to fill the gap.

accent.note: Sand is the accent on navy. Steel Blue is NOT: 3.36:1 fails AA for body text.

state.$comment: ADDED in v2.0. v1.0 defined none. A system with no state colours guarantees that someone invents them.

focus.note: 2px ring plus a 2px offset ring in the surface colour, so it reads on white and on navy alike.

link.note: Underlined. Colour alone never carries meaning.

disabled-text.note: Exempt from contrast minimums by WCAG, but kept legible on purpose.

chart.$comment: REWRITTEN in v2.0. The v1.0 rule — 'use shades within the existing blue family' — does not work and the arithmetic is in the book. Five blues give a best adjacent separation of 2.05:1 and collapse in greyscale, which is how charts print into tender packs.

emphasis.note: The one series that matters, against the rest in Mist Blue. Only on navy or in a navy-framed chart.

chart.rule: Above two categories, carry identity by direct labelling, small multiples or position — never by a third and fourth blue.

type.$comment: v1.0 named two families and six styles but no sizes, no line-heights, no measure and no scale ratio. That is a font list, not a type system.

office-fallback.$comment: CORRECTED. v1.0 specified Calibri for body and nothing for headings, so the serif — the distinctive element — simply vanished in Word and email. Georgia ships with Office on Windows and Mac.

scale.$comment: 1.25 major third. Six steps and no more.

measure.note: ADDED. Lines beyond roughly 75 characters lose the return.

headline-case.$comment: PARTIAL CHANGE from v1.0, not a reversal. v1.0 set both jumbo and main headlines in All Caps. Caps are kept where they are a graphic statement of a few words — covers, section dividers, the display step. Main headlines move to sentence case, because at headline length caps cost reading speed and cannot carry the italic accent.

eyebrow-face.$comment: UNCHANGED from v1.0. Newsreader Medium, uppercase, tracked. An earlier draft of v2.0 proposed moving this to IBM Plex; that was preference rather than defect, and it is withdrawn.

accent.rule: One accent phrase per title, Newsreader Italic.
accent.$comment: ADDED. Used throughout our material and specified nowhere in v1.0. It is the most distinctive thing the brand does, and it existed only as convention.

space.$comment: ADDED. A 4px base, so spacing is a decision from a list rather than a number someone chose.

radius.$comment: v1.0 was silent. Large radii read as consumer SaaS; this is an enterprise system.

clear-space.value: 25% of logomark height on all sides
clear-space.note: v1.0 artwork had it baked at roughly 5%.

minimum-width.note: ADDED. Below this the CONVERGED INTELLIGENCE line stops being legible before the mark does.

accessibility.$comment: Stated as the standard because it is scored in public-sector procurement in several of our markets.
